title: Start With Why
author: Simon Sinek
thesisParagraph: People are inspired to buy, work, endure inconvenience, and follow when they recognize a shared purpose before they evaluate features or incentives. Durable leadership keeps WHY, HOW, and WHAT aligned; fragile organizations substitute manipulations for meaning and win transactions without earning loyalty.

signatureMoves: states a simple leadership distinction, then reinforces it through business anecdotes and brand contrasts
capitalizes WHY, HOW, and WHAT as named conceptual layers rather than ordinary question words
uses diagrams and metaphors such as the circle, cone, megaphone, bell curve, and celery test to make abstract purpose operational
returns repeatedly to Apple, the Wright brothers, Martin Luther King Jr., Southwest Airlines, and other familiar anchors
frames claims as practical pattern recognition, moving from story to principle to business consequence
avoidMoves: does not build an academic literature review with extended caveats
does not rely on dense statistical proof beyond a few adoption-curve percentages and business outcomes
does not use literary ornament or ironic detachment
does not treat purpose as a private journal exercise divorced from hiring, marketing, culture, and operations

teachingArc: Part 1 shows why assumption-based management and manipulative sales tactics create brittle results. Part 2 introduces the Golden Circle, ties it to decision biology, and defines alignment as clarity of WHY, discipline of HOW, and consistency of WHAT. Part 3 explains how trust and early adopters create a following; Part 4 turns WHY into leadership roles, communication, and symbols; Part 5 warns that success can blur the founding cause; Part 6 reframes WHY as something discovered from origins and protected through self-competition.
